note: Party exp sharing (mob_dead and party_exp_share) and party loot (pc_takeitem and party_share_loot). The header holds the battle_config values the cases use. Each case changes only party_even_share_bonus (exp) or party_share_type (loot). Exp cases: 'players' are sample players with the melee build. 'party' is 0 for no party, or party 1 or 2. 'map' is 'same' for the monster's map or 'other' for izlude. 'dead' players have dead_sit set. 'party_exp' is the party's exp option by party number: 0 each take, 1 even share. 'damage' is the damage log in order. Each entry goes to mob_log_damage, except the last one when 'killer' is not -1: then the monster's HP is set to 1 and status_damage deals the entry's damage, which mob_damage logs in full. When 'killer' is -1, status_damage with no source kills the monster after the log is filled. 'gained' lists every pc_gainexp call during the kill, in order, with the base and job exp passed in, before pc_calcexp. 'monster_base_exp' and 'monster_job_exp' are the monster's mob_db exp after the server rates. Loot cases: one Jellopy (amount 1) is dropped with map_addflooritem and taken with pc_takeitem by 'picker'. All players on the same map stand on the item's cell. 'first', 'second' and 'third' are the looter player indices, or -1 for none. 'first_tick', 'second_tick' and 'third_tick' are their protection ticks in milliseconds after the drop, and 'at' is the pick-up time after the drop. 'party_item' is the party's item option: bit 1 shares pick-up priority, bit 2 shares the item among members. 'share_type' is battle_config.party_share_type. 'slot' is the player's party member slot. 'inventory_full' players have every inventory slot taken, so pc_additem fails. 'itemc_before' and 'itemc_after' are the picker's party round robin counter (party_data.itemc), or -1 when the picker has no party. 'taken' is what pc_takeitem returned. It is also true when no one could hold the item. 'floor_cleared' is true when the item left the floor. 'receiver' is the player whose inventory gained the item, or -1. 'candidates' are the player indices in rAthena's order for the first random pick, and 'drawn' is each index rnd_value(0, count-1) drew. When a drawn candidate cannot hold the item, rAthena moves the last candidate into its place and draws again from one fewer.
